title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: GDP growth forecast 2025
sections.summary: MTI has again maintained its 2025 GDP growth forecast at between 1% and 3% in the latest January release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the latest January release, MTI has again maintained the gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast for 2025 as between 1% to 3%.

sections.label: MTI research and innovation plans
sections.summary: The question asks about MTI's plans to grow the research and innovation ecosystem, support semiconductors and biomedical sciences, and attract innovative companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this regard, can I ask what are MTI's plans to grow our research and innovation ecosystem; and, in particular, to support the development of sectors, such as semi-conductors and biomedical sciences?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can MTI share how it intends to attract and support high-performing, innovative companies into Singapore?

sections.label: Enterprise Compute Initiative
sections.summary: The new $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative brings in major cloud service providers to help companies access and embed AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The new $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative brings in major cloud service providers to help companies access and embed AI solutions in their business, including computing power with the help of expert consultancy services.

sections.label: Scenarios for Singapore's economy
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister what possible scenarios Singapore could face and how they will impact us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: He mentioned that as a small and open economy, Singapore will certainly feel the impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Minister what are the possible scenarios that Singapore could face and how it will impact us?

sections.label: Singapore's economic positioning and reserves
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore has strengthened itself over 60 years and must re-evaluate its economic competitive positioning to stay viable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: When Singapore became Independent in 1965, we indeed have very few or have weak cards to play.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: That is why over the last 60 years, we have been so single-minded and obsessed about strengthening Singapore; whether it is in security, economy, social unity, among others and, importantly, to always be in a strong fiscal position and to have strong reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This is so that Singapore will always have strong cards to play to defend our national interest and not to be dictated or at the mercy of others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And importantly also, to have the means to mitigate the impact and fallout come what may.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the new, more-contested and technology-driven economic landscape, we again need to re-evaluate our economic competitive positioning and to up the game.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I hope that we will always be bold, as a country, to seek new growth frontiers and continually look to remake and invigorate our economy to stay viable, so that Singapore will always have strong cards to play to survive and to thrive in these extraordinary times.

sections.label: US-China trade tensions
sections.summary: Ongoing US-China trade tensions with mutual tariffs will cause supply chain shifts and trickle-down effects on Singapore's economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The ongoing US-China trade tensions which have seen both nations imposing trade tariffs against each other will cause supply chain shifts and trickle-down effects on our economy.

sections.label: US tariffs on three countries
sections.summary: Recently announced US tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China are expected to raise tariff costs in those countries by $250 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recently announced US tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China are expected to place significant barriers on trade, increasing tariff costs in the three countries by a whopping $250 billion.

sections.label: Impact on Singapore hub economy
sections.summary: For Singapore, the impact on trade, value proposition and FDI attractiveness in manufacturing, biopharma and the digital economy will be impacted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For a hub economy like Singapore, the impact on trade and our value proposition and attractiveness as a place for foreign direct investment (FDI) in key sectors like manufacturing, biopharma and the digital economy will be impacted.

sections.label: US-China trade war tariffs
sections.summary: The US-China trade war resulted in increased tariffs on approximately $1.4 trillion in imports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The US-China trade war resulted in increased tariffs on approximately $1.4 trillion in imports.

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: Singapore's manufacturing sector accounts for about 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Singapore's manufacturing sector accounts for about 20% of our GDP.

sections.label: Manufacturing cornerstone of economy
sections.summary: Manufacturing contributes nearly 20% of GDP and provides over 450,000 jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Manufacturing remains a cornerstone of our economy, contributing nearly 20% of our GDP and providing over 450,000 good jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singapore's free trade agreements
sections.summary: Singapore's 15 bilateral and 12 regional Free Trade Agreements are key to its open, trade-driven economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our 15 bilateral and 12 regional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) are key to our open economy driven by trade in goods and services.

sections.label: US tariffs on imports
sections.summary: The US has announced a host of tariffs on imports from China, Canada and Mexico as Trump 2.0 starts this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As Trump 2.0 starts this year, the US has already announced a host of tariffs on imports from China, Canada and Mexico.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
sections.summary: The Johor-Singapore SEZ covers nine flagship areas and contemplates centralising manufacturing in six named locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The announcement of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (SEZ) agreed between Singapore and Malaysia is an exciting prospect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Covering a range of different economic sectors over nine "flagship" areas, the SEZ contemplates centralising manufacturing activities in Pengerang, Pasir Gudang, Tanjung Pelepas, Iskandar Puteri, Sedenak and Senai-Skudai.

sections.label: Regulations against planned obsolescence
sections.summary: The speaker proposes regulations against planned obsolescence and right-to-repair laws to cut waste, costs and environmental damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Chairman, we should consider having regulations against plan of obsolescence of products to prevent products which are designed with limited lifespan, as they increase waste, consumer costs and environmental damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We should introduce regulations providing for the right to repair, as such laws can encourage longer product life cycles and reduce waste and carbon footprint.

sections.label: Extended Producer Responsibility scheme limits
sections.summary: Singapore's Extended Producer Responsibility scheme covers e-waste disposal but not non-electronic products that also emit carbon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singapore's Extended Producer Responsibility scheme holds producers accountable for e-waste disposal, but it does not cover non-electronic products, which also contribute to carbon emissions.

sections.label: France anti-waste law
sections.summary: France's anti-waste law includes measures such as repairability indexes for electronic devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In France, their anti-waste law includes measures, such as repairability indexes for electronic devices.

sections.label: National Repairability Framework proposal
sections.summary: A National Repairability Framework would require manufacturers to disclose expected product lifespan and provide standardised repairability ratings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A National Repairability Framework requiring manufacturers to disclose the expected lifespan of their products and provide standardised repairability ratings would greatly enhance consumer protection.

sections.label: Overarching consumer protection body proposed
sections.summary: The speaker says an overarching body to set and enforce consumer standards and protections is desirable over the current sector-specific, fragmented approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some of my own residents were saved from losses due to interventions during ongoing transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, as consumers continue to lose a record amount of money to scams across a wider range of sectors and to increasingly sophisticated criminals, an overarching body to set and enforce standards and protections for consumers will be desirable over the current sector-specific and somewhat fragmented approach.

sections.label: CCCS as central consumer body
sections.summary: With investment and job scams making up 29% and 14% of 2024 scam losses, the speaker believes CCCS is best placed for a central consumer rights role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With investment scams and job scams making up 29% and 14% of all scam losses in 2024, the Government will constantly have to play catch up with evolving scam methodologies across various sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Accordingly, I believe that the Competition and Consumer Commission (CCCS) is best placed to take on such a central role with a focus on consumer rights.

sections.label: E-commerce complaints hit all-time high
sections.summary: CASE's annual complaints statistics showed e-commerce complaints reached an all-time high in 2024, surpassing the COVID-19 pandemic peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the annual complaints statistics released by CASE showed that e-commerce complaints reached an all-time high in 2024, surpassing even the peak caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: SME Pro-Enterprise Office established
sections.summary: Following Alliance for Action on Business Competitiveness feedback, Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling announced the SME Pro-Enterprise Office to tackle regulatory challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, as a result of feedback from the Alliance for Action on Business Competitiveness, Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling announced the establishment of the SME Pro-Enterprise Office (PEO) to tackle regulatory challenges and strengthen Singapore’s pro-business environment.

sections.label: Alliance consultations and PEO launch
sections.summary: After nine months of consultations, the alliance produced 27 recommendations, and the SME Pro-Enterprise Office under Enterprise Singapore was launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over nine months of consultations with more than 100 business leaders, 13 trade associations and 17 public agencies, this alliance produced 27 recommendations to tackle key challenges in manpower, land use and regulatory frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Alongside this, as mentioned earlier, an Inter-Ministerial Committee on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review was established under Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A key outcome is the launch of the SME Pro-Enterprise Office under Enterprise Singapore, which is being welcomed by all trade associations and SMEs.

sections.label: IMC and SME Pro-Enterprise Office
sections.summary: The IMC for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review was established in April 2024 to improve regulatory efficiency and ease compliance burdens, especially for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The IMC for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review was established in April 2024 to improve regulatory efficiency and to ease compliance burdens, especially for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: MTI also announced the establishment of the SME Pro-Enterprise Office (PEO).

sections.label: Long-Term Investment and Private Credit Funds
sections.summary: Asks how the Long-Term Investment Fund and Private Credit Growth Fund will help address challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How will the Long-Term Investment Fund and Private Credit Growth Fund help address these challenges?

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Rules Review Bodies
sections.summary: The Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review and SME Pro-Enterprise Office were launched in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review and SME Pro-Enterprise Office (PEO) were launched in 2024.

sections.label: Partnerships for Capability Transformation Scheme
sections.summary: Asks the utilisation rate of the Partnerships for Capability Transformation Scheme relative to its budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Partnerships for Capability Transformation Scheme fosters such partnerships, but what is the utilisation rate of the scheme relative to its budget?

sections.label: Tourism 2040 Roadmap
sections.summary: Last year, the Singapore Tourism Board announced the Tourism 2040 roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) announced the Tourism 2040 roadmap.

sections.label: Singapore Economic Resilience Priorities
sections.summary: Singapore's economic resilience depends on fostering innovation, low-carbon transition, strengthening local enterprises and revitalising tourism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore’s economic resilience depends on fostering innovation, transition to a low-carbon economy, strengthening local enterprises and revitalising tourism.

sections.label: Singapore Global Innovation Index Ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranks fourth in WIPO's Global Innovation Index, behind Switzerland, Sweden and the United States.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have built a strong reputation as a trusted, forward-looking hub for technology and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is reflected in the World Intellectual Property Organization's (WIPO's) Global Innovation Index, where Singapore ranks fourth globally, behind only Switzerland, Sweden and the United States.

sections.label: Singapore startup ecosystem ranking rise
sections.summary: Singapore rose from sixteenth in 2020 to seventh in 2024 in the Global Startup Ecosystem Ranking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our startup ecosystem continues to gain global recognition, with Singapore rising from sixteenth position in 2020 to seventh in 2024 in the Global Startup Ecosystem Ranking.

sections.label: Private Credit Growth Fund question
sections.summary: A question asks how the new $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund will nurture high-growth enterprises and keep them in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: How will the new $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund contribute to nurturing high-growth enterprises and keep them anchored in Singapore?

sections.label: RIE2025 innovation budget allocation
sections.summary: The RIE2025 plan allocates $28 billion, about 1% of GDP, to strengthen technological and scientific capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Through our annual budget, we have consistently invested in innovation as a driver of growth, with the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025) plan allocating $28 billion – approximately 1% of GDP – to strengthen our technological and scientific capabilities.

sections.label: MNEs reassessing global supply chains
sections.summary: Rising protectionism, trade realignments and economic nationalism prompt some MNEs to reassess supply chains, restructure Asian operations and diversify investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Rising protectionism, global trade realignments and economic nationalism are prompting some MNEs to reassess their global supply chains, restructure their Asian operations and diversify investments.

sections.label: Commercialising university research patents
sections.summary: A question asks how the Ministry can accelerate commercialisation of university patents and prioritise local enterprises in licensing them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore universities and research institutes produce a wealth of intellectual property (IP) in the form of patents, which hold significant potential to drive innovation and economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How can the Ministry work with universities, businesses and other stakeholders to accelerate the commercialisation of these research patents, ensuring that their benefits are retained within our local economy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, are there plans to enhance existing initiatives or introduce new measures that prioritise local enterprises in acquiring and licensing university patents at accessible rates?

sections.label: Budget 2025 enterprise support schemes
sections.summary: Budget 2025 extended the enhanced Market Readiness Grant and Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation, and enhanced the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In Budget 2025, several of the schemes, such as the enhanced Market Readiness Grant, that helps SMEs defray the costs of overseas market promotion, business development and market setup and the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme that allows businesses to claim a 200% tax deduction on qualifying market expansion and investment development expenses, have been extended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Enterprise Financing Scheme has also been enhanced.

sections.label: Private Credit Growth Fund
sections.summary: The newly announced $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund provides more financing options for high-growth companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The newly announced $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund is a welcome initiative to provide more financing options for high-growth companies.

sections.label: Career Conversion Programme enhancement
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government would enhance the Career Conversion Programme with up to 90% salary support, capped at $7,500 monthly, for redeployed workers post-merger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider enhancing the Career Conversion Programme to provide up to 90% salary support, capped at $7,500 per month, specifically for workers who need to be redeployed post-merger?

sections.label: Enterprise Compute Initiative structure
sections.summary: The question asks how the $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative announced at Budget will be structured to give SMEs capabilities and technical support for digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, how will the $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative announced at Budget be structured to provide SMEs with the capabilities and technical support they need to accelerate their digital transformation?

sections.label: Support schemes utilisation and eligibility
sections.summary: The passage asks about utilisation of existing support schemes and AI adoption, eligibility criteria for the Enterprise Compute Initiative, and proposes upfront financial support for vendors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: What is the rate of utilisation of these various existing support schemes and adoption of AI by businesses in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: For the new Enterprise Compute Initiative announced in Budget 2025, what are the criteria for businesses to be eligible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, Enterprise Singapore plays a crucial role in supporting our SMEs through various grants and schemes in their green transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the current reimbursement model creates uncertainty in capital recovery, discouraging SMEs from making much-needed investments in sustainable equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To improve accessibility, I propose that Enterprise Singapore provide upfront financial support, particularly for vendors who have already cleared the agency’s onboarding criteria.

sections.label: Heartland merchants scheme interest
sections.summary: About 40 heartland merchants have expressed intent to leverage on this scheme as of September 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Since its announcement, it is heartening to know that about 40 heartland merchants have expressed intent to leverage on this scheme as of September 2024.

sections.label: Tourism receipts increase
sections.summary: Tourism receipts reached S$22.4 billion between January and September 2024, a 10% increase over the same period in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: Tourism receipts reached S$22.4 billion between January and September 2024, a 10% increase compared to the same period in 2023.

sections.label: JS-SEZ arts community support
sections.summary: MP asks whether initiatives will support the arts community overseas, noting arts and creative industries are not among the JS-SEZ's 11 identified economic sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, my first cut has to do with the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and whether specific initiatives have been put in place or will be put in place in order to support the arts community in opportunities overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the arts and creative industries have not been expressly included in the 11 identified economic sectors of focus for economic cooperation.

sections.label: Artist-friendly JS-SEZ plans
sections.summary: MP asks whether plans exist to facilitate artist-friendly rental agreements, co-working studio spaces, or grant schemes for creative businesses expanding within the zone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the JS-SEZ’s goal of enhancing cross-border collaboration, are there plans to facilitate artist-friendly rental agreements, co-working studio spaces, or grant schemes to encourage creative businesses to expand within the zone?

sections.label: Singapore music festivals decline
sections.summary: A Straits Times article noted Baybeats, Mosaic Music Festival and Singapore International Jazz Festival debuted between the 2000s and mid-2010s, but only Baybeats remains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Straits Times article in October last year noted that many events, A Straits Times article in October last year noted that many events, such as Baybeats, Mosaic Music Festival and the Singapore International Jazz Festival, all debuted between the 2000s and mid-2010s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, of all of these festivals, only Baybeats remains.

sections.label: Yuewen and Sunda festivals
sections.summary: The Yuewen Music Festival debuted in Singapore in December 2024, and the Sunda Music Festival is scheduled for April this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Yuewen Music Festival debuted in Singapore in December 2024, and the Sunda Music Festival is scheduled to take place in April this year.

sections.label: Standardised sustainability reporting software
sections.summary: MP asks whether the Government would consider developing national standardised software with data templates to streamline sustainability reporting and reduce compliance burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: To further support businesses, would the Government consider developing a national standardised software with data templates to streamline sustainability reporting and reduce compliance burdens?

sections.label: Data centre power demand growth
sections.summary: Goldman Sachs Research projects global data centre power demand to rise 50% by 2027 and up to 165% by 2030 versus 2023 levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: According to the Goldman Sachs Research, global power demand from data centers is projected to increase by 50% by 2027, with a potential rise of up to 165% by 2030 compared to 2023 levels.

sections.label: Singapore net-zero emissions commitment
sections.summary: Singapore is committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 through its LEDS, Green Plan 2030, carbon tax and transport electrification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Singapore is committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Singapore has made significant actions through strategies outlined in Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy (LEDS) and Singapore Green Plan 2030 as well as the implementation of measures, such as the carbon tax and electrification of transport.

sections.label: Nuclear energy study and Future Energy Fund
sections.summary: Budget 2025 announced Singapore will study deploying nuclear energy, focusing on small modular reactors, with the Future Energy Fund supporting this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In Budget 2025, Prime Minister Wong announced that to meet our growing energy needs and to reduce carbon emissions, Singapore will study the potential of deploying nuclear energy and build capabilities in nuclear energy with a focus on small modular reactors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Future Energy Fund reinforces our commitment to a low carbon, sustainable and secure energy future.

sections.label: 2035 emissions target and clean energy imports
sections.summary: Singapore pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions to 45-50 million tonnes by 2035 and raise clean energy imports to six gigawatts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore has pledged to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes by 2035, which will put it on course to reach net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Part of our strategy is to increase our clean energy imports from four gigawatts to six gigawatts by 2035, which is projected to meet one-third of our energy needs.

sections.label: Natural gas, LNG hub and hydrogen
sections.summary: Natural gas powers about 95% of Singapore's electricity, and Singapore is a leading LNG and bunkering hub with hydrogen-ready power plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Presently, natural gas has been powering around 95% of Singapore's electricity supply while coal, petroleum products and other energy products like biomass and solar supplied the rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Singapore has also established itself as a leading LNG and bunkering hub in Asia, backed by investments including our LNG plant that can store more than 300,000 cubic metres of LNG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As for hydrogen, besides the construction of hydrogen-ready power plants, can MTI share what are our hydrogen strategy plans and what are the use cases for Singapore over the next five to 10 years?

sections.label: GDP growth and core inflation
sections.summary: GDP grew by 4.4% compared to 1.8% in 2023, and core inflation fell from 4.2% in 2023 to 2.7% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 4.4%, compared to 1.8% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Core inflation came down from 4.2% in 2023 to 2.7% in 2024.

sections.label: Economic growth and inflation outlook
sections.summary: Singapore expects its economy to expand by about 1% to 3% this year with core inflation at about 1% to 2%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Singapore can also capitalise on the shifts in production and supply chains to attract new investments and strengthen our position as a key node in the reconfigured trade flows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We expect our economy to expand by about 1% to 3% this year and inflation to stay moderated, with core inflation at about 1% to 2%, barring major disruptions.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore signed the Agreement on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone with Malaysia this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As a business hub, our success depends on staying well-connected to the region and to the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This year, we signed the Agreement on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) with Malaysia.

sections.label: ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore will enhance digital trade and market access in ASEAN, and is making progress to substantially conclude DEFA negotiations this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Second, we will continue to enhance digital trade and improve market access for our companies operating in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are making progress to substantially conclude our negotiations on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) this year.

sections.label: NSTIC semiconductor R&D fabrication facility
sections.summary: A*STAR will broaden NSTIC to cover more semi-conductor technologies and invest about $500 million in the NSTIC (R&D Fab) at JTC nanoSpace @ Tampines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To build on this, A*STAR will broaden NSTIC to cover more semi-conductor technologies and increase the capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will invest about $500 million to establish the NSTIC (R&D Fab), a new national semi-conductor R&D fabrication facility at JTC nanoSpace @ Tampines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The NSTIC (R&D Fab) will have an initial focus on advanced packaging, which is a key growth area in the semi-conductor industry.

sections.label: NSTIC R&D Fab industry capabilities
sections.summary: The NSTIC (R&D Fab) will scale up capacity for SMEs and the semi-conductor industry to build capabilities, commercialise technologies and create jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The NSTIC (R&D Fab) will scale up our capacity to enable similar SMEs and the broader semi-conductor industry here to build new capabilities, develop and commercialise globally-competitive technologies and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Enhanced GIA for startups
sections.summary: Singapore will enhance the GIA to support startups in various growth stages and help them accelerate speed to market and product commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We want to support more startups like Carecam to accelerate their speed to market and facilitate their product commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will enhance the GIA to support startups in various growth stages.

sections.label: EDB Global Founder Programme

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To do so, the Economic Development Board (EDB) will launch a Global Founder Programme (GFP) later this year.

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: Manufacturing makes up close to 20% of GDP and is a leading contributor to productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Manufacturing is a key pillar of our economy, comprising close to 20% of our GDP and is one of the largest contributors to productivity growth.

sections.label: KLA facility job creation

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: KLA's new facility is expected to create at least 400 jobs, in areas, such as mechanical design, materials and product testing.

sections.label: Equity and debt financing funds
sections.summary: The Government allocated over $1.8 billion in equity investment funds over five years and will introduce a Long-Term Investment Fund and a $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: First, we will introduce the Long-Term Investment Fund and deploy more than $200 million of Government capital over a longer time horizon, beyond the typical three- to seven-year timescale.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Second, we will launch a $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund (PCGF).

sections.label: CET degree with SIT
sections.summary: The Government partnered the Singapore Institute of Technology on a continuing education and training degree to upskill in-employment diploma holders in manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, we have partnered the Singapore Institute of Technology on a continuing education and training (CET) degree, to upskill in-employment diploma holders in manufacturing.

sections.label: Global Business Leaders Programme
sections.summary: Last year the Global Business Leaders Programme and the Singapore Leaders Network Fellowship were launched to equip managers for regional and global leadership roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched the Global Business Leaders Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also launched the Singapore Leaders Network (SGLN) Fellowship to equip managers with the ambition to assume regional and global leadership roles.

sections.label: Enhancing SGLN support
sections.summary: SGLN is being enhanced to better support more Singaporeans like Camy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are proud that Camy is flying the Singapore flag high.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are enhancing SGLN to better support more Singaporeans like Camy.

sections.label: Open trade and pro-business growth
sections.summary: Singapore can look ahead confidently by staying open to trade, talent and investments, keeping a pro-business environment, and strengthening its competitive edge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We can look ahead to the next bound of our economic development with confidence, by remaining open to trade, talent and investments, as well as maintaining a pro-business environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We must further strengthen our competitive edge through innovation, deepen our integration with the region and with the world, and investing in building strong enterprises and a skilled workforce.

sections.label: Singapore net-zero by 2050
sections.summary: Singapore has committed to achieve net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Singapore has committed to achieve net-zero by 2050.

sections.label: Raising solar imports ambition
sections.summary: Imports ambition is raised from four gigawatts to around six gigawatts by 2035, and the 2025 deployment target of 1.5 gigawatt-peak was met ahead of schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: They underpin new investments for the source country.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And given the substantive progress that we have made, we have raised our imports ambition from four gigawatts (GWs) to around six GWs by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As Senior Minister Teo has also shared, we achieved our 2025 deployment target of 1.5 gigawatt-peak (GWp) ahead of schedule.

sections.label: Simplified solar PV installation processes
sections.summary: Simplified processes exempt more than half of solar photovoltaic installations on metal-roofed buildings from fire separation requirements, saving eligible owners up to 30% on construction cost.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The simplified processes exempt more than half of all solar photovoltaic (PV) installations on metal-roofed buildings from fire separation requirements, allowing eligible building owners to save up to 30% on total construction cost.

sections.label: Funding low-carbon technology testbed
sections.summary: For less mature solutions, research will be strengthened and commercialisation accelerated, with $62.5 million committed for A*STAR to develop a Low-Carbon Technology Translational Testbed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the less mature solutions, we will strengthen research efforts and accelerate commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will commit $62.5 million for the A*STAR to develop a Low-Carbon Technology Translational Testbed (LCT3) that will support companies in scaling up low-carbon solutions closer to commercial development.

sections.label: Topping-up Future Energy Fund
sections.summary: To save up for these investments, the Future Energy Fund is being topped-up by $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To save up for these investments, we are topping-up the Future Energy Fund (FEF) by $5 billion.

sections.label: FEF low-carbon energy infrastructure
sections.summary: The FEF can fund studies for deploying low-carbon energy infrastructure, including small modular reactors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To address Mr Sharael Taha's question, the FEF can also be used to fund studies for the deployment of low-carbon energy infrastructure, including those needed for small modular reactors.

sections.label: CET spending FY2024
sections.summary: Government spending on CET initiatives in FY2024 is projected to exceed $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In fact, Government spending on CET initiatives in FY2024 is projected to amount to over $1 billion.

sections.label: WSG salary support cap increase
sections.summary: Since 1 April 2024, WSG raised the monthly salary support cap from $6,000 to $7,500 for eligible workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Moreover, since 1 April 2024, WSG increased the monthly salary support cap from $6,000 to $7,500 for eligible workers with up to 90% of salary support.

sections.label: RIE2025 innovation-led economy investment
sections.summary: Singapore invested $28 billion under the RIE2025 plan to develop an innovation-led economy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We must continue developing an innovation-led economy, as Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong has shared.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore invested $28 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025) plan.

sections.label: R&D GDP and jobs growth
sections.summary: GDP contribution from firms with R&D activities grew from 15% to 24% between 2012 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The GDP contribution from firms with R&D activities grew from around 15% of GDP to 24% over a 10-year period from 2012 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The number of R&D jobs increased by 7.6% from 2021 to 2022.

sections.label: A*STAR biomedical infrastructure extension
sections.summary: The Prime Minister announced an approximately $500 million effort to extend A*STAR's biomedical research infrastructure to one-north.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister announced during Budget that we are refreshing A*STAR's biomedical research infrastructure by extending it to the greater one-north area.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is an approximately $500 million effort, which will strengthen our biomedical R&D ecosystem in two ways.

sections.label: Land Intensification Allowance extension
sections.summary: The Land Intensification Allowance scheme will be extended and enhanced to unlock new industrial space and support businesses in intensifying land use.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We support businesses to intensify land use and to be more productive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will extend and enhance the Land Intensification Allowance (LIA) scheme to unlock new industrial space.

sections.label: JTC Flexible Lease Extension Initiative
sections.summary: JTC will introduce a five-year Flexible Lease Extension Initiative letting eligible companies on 20-year leases extend by up to two tranches of five years each.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: JTC will introduce a new five-year Flexible Lease Extension Initiative (FLEXI) to give eligible companies on JTC's 20-year leases the option to extend their leases by up to two tranches of five years each.

sections.label: Innovative spirit securing Singapore's future
sections.summary: The speaker expresses confidence that the same innovative spirit shown in today's bold steps will drive growth and secure a vibrant future for generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the next 60 years and beyond, I am confident that this same innovative spirit, as reflected in the bold steps we are taking today, will drive our continued growth and it will secure a vibrant future for generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore 2024 company support
sections.summary: In 2024 Enterprise Singapore supported over 2,300 companies, boosting projected annual revenue by $14.5 billion through productivity, internationalisation and innovation projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2024, Enterprise Singapore supported more than 2,300 companies, helping them boost their projected annual revenue by $14.5 billion through transformative projects in productivity, that is $8.2 billion; internationalisation, that is $5.5 billion; as well as innovation, that is $0.8 billion, all totalling up to the $14.5 billion I highlighted earlier.

sections.label: Financing and tax support extensions
sections.summary: The maximum EFS-TL loan quantum will be permanently doubled to $10 million, DTDi extended five years, and the $100,000 MRA Grant cap extended to 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, we will permanently double the maximum loan quantum for the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan (EFS-TL) from $5 million to $10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Second, we will extend the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDi) for the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Third, we will extend the $100,000 Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) Grant cap by one more year to 31 March 2026, because this is in response to industry feedback that many companies, many businesses have spent the last two to three years getting back on their feet after COVID-19.

sections.label: SME PEO operational date
sections.summary: The SME PEO under Enterprise Singapore, set up following the AfA's recommendation, will be fully operational from 26 March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Gan earlier, he mentioned after extensive reviews and consultations, the Committee has set out three Statements of Commitment to streamline regulatory processes and to reduce the compliance burden on businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Following the AfA's recommendation, I announced last September that this new office will be set up under Enterprise Singapore to help businesses navigate regulatory matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the SME PEO will be fully operational from 26 March this year, in 20 days' time.

sections.label: Enhanced SME Centres advisory services
sections.summary: SME Centres will be enhanced to offer a wider range of business advisory services and programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Second, we will enhance our SME Centres to offer a wider range of business advisory services and programmes.

sections.label: Our Heartlands 2025 programme
sections.summary: The $50 million Our Heartlands 2025 programme was launched in 2022, and over 17,000 heartland shops have since adopted e-payment solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To recap, in 2022, we launched the $50 million Our Heartlands 2025 programme to revitalise our heartlands and to enhance the capabilities of heartland shops, helping them transform, stay relevant and continue serving residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since then, more than 17,000 heartland shops have adopted e-payment solutions.

sections.label: Heartland shops footfall and sales
sections.summary: Participating heartland shops saw footfall and sales rise by about 20%, and Singaporeans have spent over $1 billion at about 23,000 heartland shops and hawker stalls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As a result of this programme, the heartland shops that participated shared that they have seen their footfall and their sales increase by generally about 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To date, Singaporeans have spent more than $1 billion at about 23,000 heartland shops and hawker stalls.

sections.label: Visual merchandising and Vibrant Heartlands programmes
sections.summary: An Enhanced Visual Merchandising Programme will support heartland shops with training, consultancy and shopfront makeovers, and a new Vibrant Heartlands Programme will support Merchants' Associations' placemaking activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Starting from the "inside" of our heartland shops, we will launch the Enhanced Visual Merchandising Programme to help our heartland shops refresh their stores and gain visual appeal to attract more customers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This enhanced programme will offer the heartland shops support in training, consultancy as well as makeover of their shopfronts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We are increasing the total qualifying cost by five times, from $12,000 previously to $60,000 now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: From "inside" to "outside", besides revitalising the interiors of heartland shops, we will also rejuvenate what takes place in our heartlands' neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will launch a new Vibrant Heartlands Programme for Merchants' Associations to support their placemaking activities and events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Bite-sized and pre-scoped activities would receive grant support on qualifying costs of $3,000 per application, while larger-scale customisable placemaking events would receive grant support on qualifying costs of up to $200,000 per application.

sections.label: International visitors and tourism receipts
sections.summary: Singapore welcomed 16.5 million international visitors last year, and tourism receipts for the first three quarters of 2024 reached $22.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Last year, we welcomed 16.5 million international visitors and our tourism receipts for the first three quarters of 2024 soared to a historic high of $22.4 billion.

sections.label: MICE city rankings and summits
sections.summary: Singapore hosted young leaders at the World Economic Forum's Young Global Leaders Annual Summit and has been Asia Pacific's Top Meeting City for 21 consecutive years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I also hosted young leaders at last year's World Economic Forum's Young Global Leaders Annual Summit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And true to our positioning as the World's Best MICE City, we have been Asia Pacific's Top Meeting City for an incredible 21 consecutive years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For the first time ever, Singapore also ranked second in the International Congress and Convention Association's worldwide city rankings in 2023 .

sections.label: Tourism arrivals and receipts forecast
sections.summary: This year, international visitor arrivals are expected to reach 17.0 to 18.5 million, bringing in about $29.0 to $30.5 billion in tourism receipts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In fact, this year we expect international visitor arrivals to reach between 17.0 and 18.5 million, bringing in approximately $29.0 to $30.5 billion in tourism receipts.

sections.label: Gardens by the Bay SG60 pass
sections.summary: Gardens by the Bay will launch an SG60 Wonder Blooms Pass giving citizens and residents over 60% discounts on unlimited visits to six upcoming floral displays in the Flower Dome.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For instance, Gardens by the Bay will launch an exclusive SG60 Wonder Blooms Pass for citizens and residents to enjoy over 60% discounts on unlimited visits to six stunning upcoming floral displays in our Flower Dome.

sections.label: Disney Adventure cruise ship Singapore
sections.summary: The Disney Adventure cruise ship in Singapore is starting in December.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Like on Disney Adventure cruise ship in Singapore, which is starting in December.

sections.label: ASEAN-China Free Trade Area upgrade
sections.summary: The second upgrade of the ASEAN-China Free Trade Area was substantially concluded last year, with the aim to fully conclude the upgrade this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Beyond these, we also substantially concluded the second upgrade of the ASEAN-China Free Trade Area last year and aim to fully conclude the upgrade this year.

sections.label: China-Singapore FTA upgrade protocol
sections.summary: The China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement Further Upgrade Protocol entered into force on 31 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: With China, our China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement Further Upgrade Protocol entered into force on 31 December 2024.

sections.label: SGProtein tariff savings and FTAs
sections.summary: SGProtein Pte Ltd, a plant-based protein food manufacturer, saved 8% in tariffs in the Korean market using the ASEAN-Korea FTA and the Korea-Singapore FTA; there are 27 FTAs and 43 Bilateral Investment Treaties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For instance, SGProtein Pte Ltd, which is a plant-based protein food manufacturer, enhanced its competitiveness in the Korean market with 8% saved in tariffs by using the ASEAN-Korea FTA and the Korea-Singapore FTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Today, we have 27 FTAs and 43 Bilateral Investment Treaties.

sections.label: Pacific Alliance and MERCOSUR FTAs
sections.summary: Singapore signed FTAs with the Pacific Alliance and MERCOSUR, with the Pacific Alliance agreement close to coming into effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In 2022, we signed the Pacific Alliance-Singapore FTA; and the Pacific Alliance, which comprises Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru, collectively forms the eighth largest economy in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that the FTA is very close to coming into effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We also recently signed the MERCOSUR-Singapore FTA with Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, and we are in the process of working very hard to get it ratified as well.

sections.label: Openness, competitiveness and government support
sections.summary: Singapore must stay open and connected, sharpen its edge through innovation, enterprises and people, with Government support for businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Our success as a nation depends on us continuing to be open and connected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And therefore, to stay competitive, we must sharpen our edge by fostering innovation, building strong enterprises and investing in our people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Government will support our businesses as they navigate the ever-changing currents of the global economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: By building upon our strong foundations, we will enhance connectivity, expand opportunities and strengthen Singapore's role as a gateway for people, trade and capital flow.

sections.label: Preparing for difficult external environment
sections.summary: Singapore should deepen its value proposition and remain a reliable, consistent partner amid an increasingly difficult external environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, I must say that I wish a global trade war will not happen, but we must always be prepared because the external environment, as I said, will become increasingly difficult and challenging for us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But what Singapore should do is to continue to deepen our value proposition for businesses and for our trading partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We must continue to be a reliable, consistent partner with other countries so that we will continue to be a valued player in the global economy.

sections.label: Singapore's role in US-China relations
sections.summary: Singapore hopes to continue to play a constructive role between the United States and China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Member talked about US-China relationship and how Singapore can play a role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We hope to be able to continue to play a constructive role between the two countries.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore tariff finder tool
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore developed a tariff finder tool giving information on import duties, formalities, FTA preferential duties and rules of origin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The first is we have a tariff finder tool now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That was developed by Enterprise Singapore, and the example that I gave earlier, SGProtein, can access, through this tariff finder tool, crucial information on import duties and formalities, FTA preferential duties and rules of origin for potential export market.

sections.label: Local content and Centre for Future of Trade
sections.summary: The step helps demonstrate local content and qualify for FTA benefits, and MTI and Enterprise Singapore launched CFOTI last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And this is a very crucial step because it helps to demonstrate local content and to qualify for FTA benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I also wanted to highlight that MTI and Enterprise Singapore also, again working with SBF, has launched a new Centre for Future of Trade and Investment (CFOTI) just last year.

sections.label: Private Credit Growth Fund
sections.summary: The passage states a second clarification concerns the establishment of the $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second clarification is in regard to the establishment of the $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund.

sections.label: SME CEO discussions
sections.summary: The speaker joined other ministers in hosting discussions with over 140 SME chief executive officers and chief experience officers to understand pain points and improve regulatory agility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In the last few months, I joined him as well as Minister Shanmugam, Minister Tan See Leng, Minister Desmond Lee and Minister Chee Hong Tat in hosting discussions with more than 140 chief executive officers and chief experience officers of SMEs to continue to understand, sector by sector, if there are any pain points or any areas that we can look at to further improve the whole-of-Government regulatory agility.

sections.label: NSTIC advanced packaging focus
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng will respond on geothermal energy, and the facility expands A*STAR's NSTIC to focus first on advanced packaging for semiconductors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I will ask Minister Tan See Leng to respond to the geothermal energy source.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This facility really is an expansion of the existing NSTIC facility run by A*STAR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The idea is to focus first on advanced packaging because advanced packaging is a foundational technology for many of the advanced technologies for semi-conductor, in order to pack more and more components into the chips.

sections.label: R&D investment, NSTIC focus
sections.summary: The passage states it is important to encourage R&D investment by MNCs and local SMEs, and NSTIC (R&D Fab) will focus first on advanced packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: That is why it is important for us to encourage investment in the R&D in this particular aspect of the technology, particularly, not just the multinational corporations (MNCs), but also the local SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will allow the NSTIC (R&D Fab) to focus, first, on advanced packaging.

sections.label: Airborne geothermal survey
sections.summary: The passage states this differs from NTU's study on conventional geothermal potential, and an airborne survey of geothermal energy potential commences this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This is actually quite different from NTU's study, which is conventional geothermal potential.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I am actually pleased to update that this month, we are commencing an airborne survey of our geothermal energy potential.

sections.label: MTI, IMCS, CCCS scrutiny
sections.summary: The passage asks about MTI's interest and contribution to the IMCS and whether CCCS is looking into consumer protection and unequal bargaining power with banks, telcos and social media companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I read that MTI is also represented on that committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to understand a little bit more on what is MTI's interest and contribution so far to the work of the IMCS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second question is: of course, underlying my cut is the issue of consumer protection because as far as scams are concerned, we often find that the consumer is actually dealing with service providers like banks, telecommunications companies (telcos) and social media companies, and there is some unequal bargaining power there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to understand whether the CCCS is actually looking into this area.

sections.label: Anti-scam efforts and unfair practices
sections.summary: Anti-scam efforts are coordinated by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Scams, and CCCS can act against unfair supplier practices under CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Members have heard from Minister of State Sun Xueling, with the various tech companies and so on, as well as community partners, to tackle scams, go upstream, not just engaging the seniors, but it can affect people of all ages and all backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, the anti-scam efforts are coordinated by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Scams, which comprises representatives from MHA, Singapore Police Force, MDDI, IMDA, MAS and other public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Notwithstanding that, I want to assure the Member that where there are unfair practices by, say, suppliers being involved, CCCS can certainly take them to task under our CPFTA.

sections.label: NSTIC R&D commercialisation facilities
sections.summary: The NSTIC (R&D Fab) has facilities to help companies do R&D and commercialise it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: With regard to the R&D and the commercialisation of the R&D efforts and outcomes, the NSTIC (R&D Fab) I mentioned is one such example that has facilities to help companies to do their R&D and to commercialise the R&D.

sections.label: A*STAR and IPI commercialisation support
sections.summary: A*STAR has experience commercialising research outcomes, and IPI under Enterprise Singapore advises on IP rights and commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Because A*STAR, meaning the research centre, has a lot of experience in commercialising some of their research outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We also have IPI that is set up under Enterprise Singapore that provides advisory on particularly IP rights, whether they are making use of IP that is already available, how to take advantage of the existing IP to commercialise the IP, or to register their own IP that they have developed.

sections.label: Managing the $1 billion credit
sections.summary: The $1 billion credit is limited, so fund managers with good track records will be sought to manage it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Member also talked about the $1 billion credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I do appreciate that it is limited because it is just $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But I do agree that we need to progress very carefully and conservatively to make sure that this $1 billion is put to good use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we do intend to go out to look for fund managers with a good track record, to have experience in managing private equity, private credit and managing projects, so that we are able to leverage on the expertise of these fund managers to manage the $1 billion so that we can put it to good use.

sections.label: Renewable energy import ambition raised
sections.summary: Given progress in negotiations with neighbours, the renewable energy import ambition was raised from four to six gigawatts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the renewable energy imports, I have shared that, given the progress that we have had in our negotiations with our neighbours, we have upped the ambition from four gigawatts to six gigawatts.

sections.label: Conditional licences for generation sources
sections.summary: Conditional licences are for closer sources in the Batam, Bintan and Karimun corridor, with conditional approvals also awarded for Indochina and potentially Australia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At this particular point in time, the conditional licence that we have issued are for relatively closer source generation sources, namely, coming from the Batam, Bintan and Karimun corridor.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Member would have read in the open-source media that we have also awarded conditional approvals to further up north from Indochina and also, at the same time, potentially from Australia as well.

sections.label: Small project energy mix share
sections.summary: The project is very small and will constitute about 0.5% of the overall energy mix.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the project, because it is very small, it is going to constitute like 0.5% of our overall energy mix.
